name: Insecure direct object reference / broken object-level authorization
mental_model: An authenticated actor can name an object, but the server fails to prove that this actor may perform this action on that object.
security_property: Every object access must authorize the exact actor-object-action tuple on the server, independent of identifier shape.
root_causes: Object lookup without ownership or policy enforcement
Client-supplied ownership trusted by the server
Authorization applied to the function but not the selected object
application_shapes: Account, invoice, ticket, and message objects
signals: Object identifiers are accepted from the client
Two controlled accounts expose parallel object shapes
A cross-owner response differs from a clean denial

hypothesis_templates.statement: Under {preconditions}, {actor} may perform {action} on {object} owned by {owner}, producing {controlled_consequence} without object-level authorization.
preconditions: Both identities and the object are controlled
The exact object action is explicitly permitted
hypothesis_templates.expected_safe_behaviour: The server denies the cross-owner action without returning or changing object data.
hypothesis_templates.expected_vulnerable_behaviour: The cross-owner action succeeds against the controlled object.
hypothesis_templates.falsifier: The same actor-object-action tuple is denied while the owner control succeeds.
stop_conditions: The action would exceed the minimum controlled effect

safe_test_pattern: Use exactly two controlled identities and one synthetic object per identity; prove the owner positive control, one cross-owner attempt, and a safe denial control.
positive_controls: The owner can perform the permitted action on its own synthetic object
negative_controls: The non-owner receives a clean denial with no object data or state change
falsifiers: The non-owner is denied for the exact object action
The apparent object belongs to a shared or intentionally accessible scope

minimum_evidence.description: Exact cross-owner response or state difference for one synthetic object.
Controlled identity and ownership manifest binding actor, owner, object, and action.
Owner positive control and safe cross-owner denial control.
Clean two-account repeat with the same ownership oracle and receipt-bound inputs.
Human statement bounded to the exact controlled confidentiality, integrity, or availability effect.

common_false_positives: The tested identity actually holds an inherited or delegated permission
impact_boundaries: Identifier predictability is not evidence of broken authorization
One controlled read does not prove broad enumeration, modification, or account takeover
minimum_impact_rules: Use two owned identities and synthetic objects only
Do not enumerate or access third-party objects
remediation: Enforce server-side actor-object-action authorization on every object operation
Derive tenant and ownership constraints from trusted server state
Test horizontal and vertical authorization paths
programme_policy_considerations: Never strengthen proof with third-party data
lessons: The ownership oracle, safe denial control, and receipt-bound evidence must be evaluated together; a response alone is insufficient.

revisions.summary: Applied the Milestone 4 proposal: two-account ownership oracle, safe denial control, and receipt-backed evidence pattern.
